entries.title: name the instantiation, not the template, in new-expression diagnostics and the checked dump
entries.body:
A constructor-argument or arity error on a generic class now names the
instantiation the program wrote: ``Argument 1 of `new Box<i32>`: expected
i32, got string`` rather than `` `new Box` ``, matching the method-call
labels (`Box<i32>.set`) and the constructor's own `Box<i32>.constructor`.
A non-generic class reads as it did.

`--emit-checked` now prints the callee of a generic `new`
(`callee 17:13 new Box<i32> -> @Box$i32.constructor`). The dump used to
look the class up by its written name in the struct registry, which a
template is not in; it now reads the constructor `checkNew` records in
`nodeCallees` and names its owning class. The owner rather than the
expression's type, because a `new` whose value converts to an interface
has the interface's type.

The `Instantiation.template` and `owner` comments now say that a generic
method of a generic class has both set.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: the registry check counts every fragment line, and wp15 names its benchmark
entries.body:
`codeFor` in `self/codes.ts` reads each table as one flat array and steps
through it by two, so a fragment added without its code line shifts every
later pairing, and messages from there on get their neighbour's code. The
pair reader skips such a line rather than failing on it, so
`scripts/gen-diagnostic-codes.mjs --check` used to pass it as long as
`RULE_COUNT` was left alone. It now counts the strings in each table on their
own and requires twice the pairs. It also requires the `NL9xxx` codes to run
from `NL9001` with no gap. Each error names the table.

`--check` takes an optional path, and `tests/run.js` uses it to check three
broken copies of the live registry: a stray fragment in each table, and a
gap in NL9xxx. The previous check passes all three.

`docs/wp15-performance.md` §2c now says which program, box and statistic its
756 ms / 305 ms / 2.48x table was measured with. It names
`bench/hoist_field.ts` as the program that re-derives the figure, and points
at the reconciliation later in the section. The NL9010 note no longer implies
that a class which `implements` an interface has its whole layout fixed. Only
the interface's prefix is fixed; the fields after it are the author's to
order. Whether to warn about that suffix stays open in #108.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: same-named interfaces and classes across modules keep their identity
entries.body:
**An interface is a declaration, not a name (#173).** The implicit
class-to-interface conversion (`coercesTo` in `self/structs.ts`) compared
the wanted interface's name with the names in the class's `implements`
clause. A struct type is interned by name, so a module that declared its own
`interface Shape` accepted an imported `Circle` that implements a different
`Shape`. It then read `Circle`'s layout as its own `Shape`'s, which printed
garbage or ran out of memory. The conversion now asks
`implementsDeclaration`, the test #167 gave constraints, so it is refused
(NL2185). Importing the very `Shape` that `Circle` implements still converts.
`checkImplements` still looks up by name. That lookup is sound because it
runs in the module that resolved the names, and a comment now says why.

**Every duplicate-symbol refusal has a code (#174).** The four wordings of
the whole-program duplicate-symbol rule were `NL0000` under `--json`. Each
now has a code: NL3024 and NL3025 for an exported function (across the
program, or within one package), and NL3026 and NL3027 for a private one.
A constructor or method is a symbol named after its class. When two
same-named classes both declare one, the refusal now names the class, the
member and both files instead of the symbol `Base.constructor`: NL3022
across the program, NL3023 within a package. Two same-named classes with
fields alone still compile; that wider identity gap is #193. The uncoded
backlog in `tests/run.js` goes from five to two.

The comment on `collectStructMembers` stated its one-diagnostic-per-
declaration rule in terms of stage0, and gave it an expiry at R6. It now
states the rule as this compiler's own. Behaviour is unchanged.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: a function whose unproven charCodeAt can panic is not willreturn
entries.body:
`s.charCodeAt(i)` with an index the bounds walk cannot prove branches to
`nish_panic_index`, which is `noreturn`, exactly as an unproven `a[i]` does.
The attribute fixpoint was told so for `a[i]` but not for `charCodeAt`:
`stringConstructCallees` returned no callee for it, so the function and every
caller up to `nish_main` kept `willreturn`. Under the speed profile LLVM used
that to delete the panic, and a program whose `main` always indexes past the
end of a string printed its first line and exited with garbage instead of
`index out of range: 5 >= 0` and exit 1.

`stringConstructCallees` now takes the call's `nodeProvenIndex` verdict and
names `nish_panic_index` under the condition `emitCharCodeAt` emits the check
with: not proven, and not `--unchecked-indexing`. A proven `charCodeAt` still
emits no call and keeps `willreturn`.

An audit of every other emission of a `noreturn` runtime symbol
(`nish_panic_index` from `a[i]` and `pop`, `nish_panic_slice`,
`nish_panic_div`, and `nish_exit` from `panic`, `process.exit` and `expect`)
found each already reported to the fixpoint; `charCodeAt` was the one gap.
metrics: self/ IR 10368744 -> 10370381 bytes (+0.02%); one function in self/ loses willreturn; compiling self/compile.ts unchanged within noise (~400 ms)
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: bounds proofs see continue edges, lazy Result arguments and whole-record stores
entries.body:
Every access the bounds proof (`self/bounds.ts`) or the loop header hoist
(`self/emit_arrays.ts`) leaves unchecked is now in range on every edge
that reaches it. Each of the following let a program read or write past
an array or a string with no panic.

- **`continue` edges (#181).** A `continue` jumps to the `for` update or
  the `do/while` condition with its branch's effects applied, but the walk
  judged the update or condition in the end-of-body state. It now keeps a
  per-loop frame of the states at each `continue` and intersects them in.
  An inner loop's `continue` never reaches an outer loop's update.
- **`break` edges.** A `for` or `while` condition that re-establishes a
  fact, followed by a body that changes it and `break`s, left the fact
  alive after the loop. `break` states now join into the post-loop state;
  a `switch` opens its own frame.
- **Lazy `Result` arguments (#182).** `r.unwrapOr(d)` and `r.expect(m)`
  evaluate the argument only on the `Err` path; the walk now treats it
  that way instead of as always evaluated.
- **Whole-record element stores (#180).** Storing a record into an array
  of inline records rewrites it in place. The header hoist lifted a path
  through such a record out of the loop anyway. The proof and the hoist
  now share one rule, scoped to the holders that can point into that
  record's slot, so paths read off classes keep their facts and hoists.
- **Generic instantiations.** The proof tables were shared by every
  instantiation of a template, so one instantiation's proof dropped the
  check in another (`walk<i32>` next to `walk<Rec>`). Each instantiation
  now carries its own tables, installed by `enterInstance`.

None of this costs a proof elsewhere: no existing `.ll` golden changed,
`std/` stays at zero performance warnings, and `self/compile.ts`
compiles to byte-identical IR.
metrics: self/compile.ts IR byte-identical before and after (1406 bounds checks); std/ 0 performance warnings
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: name the squash subject in the break-edge nish-cmp declarations
entries.body:
Four `tests/nish-cmp.js` declarations for the `arr_bounds_break_*` cases
named the subject of an intermediate commit of #190. The squash merge
dropped that subject, so neither `CHANGELOG.md` nor the pending release
notes carried it, and `nish-cmp` failed on main. They now name #190's
squash subject, as the rest of its declarations do. A declaration's
`changelog` has to name the pull request's title, because that is the only
subject a squash merge keeps.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: fail a pull request whose body carries a session link or tool attribution
entries.body:
* ci: fail a pull request whose body carries a session link or tool attribution

The PreToolUse hook `.claude/hooks/no-attribution.mjs` refuses a tool call
that would write a session link, a model name or a "Generated with" footer
into git or GitHub. It cannot see a footer the platform appends to a pull
request body after the call that opened it, which is how session links
reached five merged bodies. The new `PR body` workflow reads the body GitHub
holds and fails on the same rule.

- The pattern list moves to `.claude/hooks/attribution-patterns.mjs`, which
  the hook and `scripts/check-pr-body.mjs` both import, so there is one list.
  The hook's behaviour is unchanged.
- The script reads the body from `BODY`, never from `${{ }}` in the shell,
  names each pattern it finds and exits 1. An empty body passes.
- The workflow runs on opened, edited, reopened and synchronize, so editing
  the footer out clears the red check.
- `npm test` now runs both the hook's suite and the new one.
- `package.json` keeps the two scripts out of the npm tarball: they import
  from `.claude/`, which the tarball does not carry, and the pack check
  refuses a shipped script with an unresolvable import.

A pull request that fails this check is fixed by editing its body, never by
loosening a pattern.

Refs: #176
Tests: scripts/check-pr-body.test.mjs, .claude/hooks/no-attribution.test.mjs

* test(ci): pin the footer the platform appended to the check's own pull request

The `PR body` check failed its own pull request on the `opened` run. The
footer the platform appended there is a different shape from the one that
reached #169: an underscored "Generated by" line whose link carries the
session id. It is now a case of its own, so both shapes are pinned.

Tests: scripts/check-pr-body.test.mjs
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: NL9010 advises reordering the fields a class adds after its interface prefix
entries.body:
`NL9010`, the wasteful-struct-padding warning, used to stay silent for every class that `implements` an interface, because the interface fixes the order of its own fields. That constraint only covers the prefix. The fields a class adds after it are the author's to order, and they can still waste padding.

The warning now keeps the longest implemented interface's fields first and orders only the rest. It fires when that makes the class smaller, and names the whole order and the size it reaches, which is measured with `layoutSize`.

The suffix is ordered least-padding-first from the prefix's end offset, taking the widest field on a tie. Widest-first is optimal only from an aligned offset. After a prefix that ends at 1 or 4, narrow fields can fill the gap: `{a: i32}` followed by `b: f64, c: i32, d: f64` goes from 32 to 24 bytes as `a, c, b, d`. Every field width in the language is a power of two equal to its alignment, which is what makes the greedy walk optimal. It matched a brute-force minimum on every shape tried.

A class with no `implements` gets the same message as before, byte for byte. Generic instantiations stay silent, and std/ stays at zero performance warnings.

Measured: 40 → 32, 32 → 24, 56 → 40 bytes on the three pinned shapes
Refs: docs/wp15-performance.md#9, docs/LANGUAGE.md
Tests: tests/cases/perf_padding_suffix, perf_padding_suffix_gap, perf_padding_suffix_quiet
Fixes #108
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: refuse two same-named classes or interfaces in one package
entries.body:
A struct type is identified by its bare name. So two modules of one package that each declared a class or interface of the same name became one type. A value of one was accepted where the other was expected, and its fields were read at the other's offsets, with no diagnostic. A class with fields only has no member symbol, so nothing collided.

The compiler now refuses the second declaration with NL3028, naming the module that declared it first. This applies to exported and private declarations alike. A declaration is compared with the first declaration of its name in its own package before any other, so the result does not depend on which module loaded first. Two packages declaring one name keep their existing refusal (NL3009). Generic instantiations get the same per-package comparison (NL3013).

`$` is now refused in a class or interface name, as it already was in function and template names. A `class Box$i32` would otherwise be the same struct type as the instantiation `Box<i32>`.

A file named two ways is now loaded once, for example `nish main.ts ./types.ts` alongside `import … from "./types"`. Module identity is the absolute, lexically normalised path. A module's name, and every byte written, still come from the first spelling.

NL3022 and NL3023, a class member shared by two same-named classes, are now unreachable. Their numbers stay reserved.

Refs: docs/LANGUAGE.md (class and interface names, `$` in declared names, one file one module), docs/wp21-packages.md §9c
Tests: tests/link/class_clash_fields, iface_clash_private, class_dollar_name, class_dollar_name_imported, class_clash_after_package, class_clash_package_after_root, generic_class_clash_signature, generic_class_clash_after_package, root_named_twice; tests/wordings/nl3028_class_name_clash
Fixes #193
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: module and package identity is the real path
entries.body:
A module's identity is now its real path: the file the operating system
opens, with every symbolic link resolved, as in Node's resolver and in
`tsc` with `preserveSymlinks: false`. A package's identity is its real
directory. What a module is called (its IR header, its diagnostics, its
output file) is still the first spelling that reached it, so a program
with no links emits the same bytes as before.

- One file reached through a link is one module. `nish main.ts
  $PWD/types.ts` in a symlinked directory loads `types.ts` once (#198,
  case 1).
- A link followed by `..` is the file it really leads to, so
  `far/../types.ts` is compiled as its own module rather than silently
  skipped (#198, case 2).
- Two modules never share an output file. A later module whose stem is
  taken writes `<stem>_2.ll`, then `_3`, and so on, where before one
  silently overwrote the other.
- A symlinked package is one package, so pnpm's layout compiles. A
  workspace link to a directory outside `node_modules` keeps the
  package's own relative imports in that package.
- One package name found at two real directories (npm's duplicate
  copies, or a diamond) is refused with NL3029. The message names both
  directories and both versions, or `no version` for a manifest without
  one. Identity by manifest is left for later, because it could only
  turn this refusal into an acceptance.

BREAKING CHANGE: a program that compiled only because two links to one
file were two modules now either compiles as one module or is refused;
one package name at two real directories is refused with NL3029.

Closes #198
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: reserve the type name integer for ranged integers
entries.body:
`integer` is now reserved for ranged integers, `integer<Lo, Hi>`, which
are planned for 1.1. This change does not build them. The one breaking
part of ranged integers was taking the name `integer` from programs that
declare something called that. Doing it now, before the 1.0 freeze,
lets the feature itself land in 1.1 without breaking anything.

- `integer` or `integer<T>` used as a type is refused with NL2333,
  which says the name is reserved for ranged integers.
- A class, interface or function named `integer` is refused with
  NL2332. This covers generic and `declare function` forms too.
- A type alias or enum named `integer` is refused the way `type Result`
  is, because `integer` is now a built-in type name (NL2275, NL2281).
- A value named `integer`, such as a local or module constant, is
  still accepted.

`integer<0, 255>` itself remains a parse error until ranged integers
arrive, because a numeric literal cannot yet be a type argument.

BREAKING CHANGE: a program that declares a type, enum, class, interface
or function named integer is refused.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: M4, the reference is frozen and 1.0 is next
entries.body:
`docs/LANGUAGE.md` now opens with the freeze. From 1.0, a minor release
may add a rule or turn a refusal into an acceptance. Withdrawing or
narrowing an accepted construct, or changing what one means, needs a
major. The wording of a refusal may change; its diagnostic code may
not. No rule in the reference changed.

The master plan's "What remains" now describes where the project stands,
rather than keeping a running history:

- M4 is the frozen reference plus the tag. 1.0.0 is cut by merging the
  `Release-As:` trailer support (#200, pending), landing a commit that
  carries `Release-As: 1.0.0`, then merging the Release PR.
- Two breaks were taken before the freeze: the type name `integer` is
  reserved (NL2332, NL2333), so ranged integers can arrive in 1.1
  without breaking anything; and module and package identity is the
  real path (NL3029), which closes #198 and the identity half of WP21 S3.
- The one question still open for 1.0 is WP22 stage D (rejecting
  `function` definitions). It withdraws an accepted construct, so it
  either lands before 1.0.0 or waits for a major. Whether it happens at
  all is still undecided.
- 1.1 begins with the data-parallel call from the threads plan (wp29),
  where the largest measured speedup in the plan is: 3.96x on four
  cores. Ranged integers (WP31 W1–W4) follow.

CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md state both halves of the version rule: before
1.0 a break moves the minor, and from 1.0 it moves the major. The wp15,
wp20, wp22 and wp29 notes and the docs index are updated to agree.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: Nish stays on 0.x until its owner declares 1.0
entries.body:
1.0 is not scheduled. The project stays on 0.x until its owner says
otherwise, so the docs no longer describe the tag as next.

- `docs/LANGUAGE.md` opens with the stability rule for both states. On
  0.x any minor release may change the language, and a change that
  withdraws or narrows an accepted construct is marked breaking. From
  1.0, a minor may only add a rule or turn a refusal into an acceptance.
  Diagnostic codes are stable in either state.
- The master plan's M4 row reads "not scheduled", and "What remains" no
  longer counts down to a tag. Work that was labelled 1.1 is now "Next":
  the data-parallel call first, then ranged integers. WP22 stage D stays
  the one open language question.
- CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md tell contributors and agents not to propose or
  cut 1.0.0, and not to add a `Release-As:` trailer.
- The wp15, wp20, wp22, wp23, wp29 and wp31 notes and the docs index
  drop the "1.1" and "before the freeze" wording.

No rule in the reference changed.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: a Release-As trailer chooses the next version
entries.body:
* build(release): a Release-As trailer chooses the next version

The release train computes the next version from the commit types, and
before 1.0 a breaking change moves the minor, so 1.0.0 was a number the
train could never propose. A `Release-As: X.Y.Z` trailer on any commit
merged since the last tag now makes the Release PR propose that version,
and that trailer is how 1.0.0 gets cut: a human merges a commit carrying
`Release-As: 1.0.0`, and the open `chore(release)` pull request is
re-titled and re-bumped to it.

The trailer can only raise the version. The version the commits imply
is a floor: a trailer below it (a downgrade, or a patch where a `feat`
asks for the minor) stops `changelog-gen.mjs --next` with a message
naming the trailer, its commit and the floor, and so does a value that
is not exactly `X.Y.Z`. When several commits carry one, the highest
wins. `--next` is the line the workflow reads for the changelog JSON,
the version bump and the pull request title, so the chosen version
reaches all of them. The trailer comes off the entry's body in the
changelog record, as `Refs:` does.

From 1.0 on, nothing changes: the existing rule already moves the major
on a breaking change, which answers the old "reconsider at 1.0" note.

Refs: docs/wp12-release.md#release-procedure
Tests: scripts/changelog-gen.test.mjs

* refactor(release): keep one version representation in nextVersion

`impliedVersion` returns the version as a `[major, minor, patch]` triple,
so the floor comparison uses it directly instead of formatting it to a
string and parsing it back. The test counts its checks as it runs them
rather than hard-coding the total. No behaviour change.

Tests: scripts/changelog-gen.test.mjs

* fix(release): refuse two Release-As trailers on one commit that disagree

A second `Release-As:` line in one commit body used to overwrite the
first without a word, so which version a commit asked for depended on
line order. One commit asking for two versions has not said which it
means, so `--next` now refuses it, naming both values and the commit,
as it refuses a malformed value. Two that agree are one request.

The test also removes its throwaway repositories on every path, not
only when every case finishes normally.

Refs: docs/wp12-release.md#release-procedure
Tests: scripts/changelog-gen.test.mjs

* docs(release): say what each Release-As refusal names

The malformed and disagreeing-trailer refusals name the trailer and the
commit but not the floor, and neither can be fixed by a later commit.
The release procedure now says what each of the three refusals names.

Refs: docs/wp12-release.md#release-procedure
